newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian bonds remain buoyed on inflation hopes.
newsitem.headline: Australian bonds remain buoyed on inflation hopes.

text.p: *Australian 10-year bond yields closed at their lowest level since February 1994 following a strong rally in U.S. Treasuries on Wednesday and ahead of next week's key inflation report.
*Ten-year bond futures eyeing all time high of 93.630.
Australian 10-year bond yields closed at their lowest level since February 1994 following a strong rally in U.S. Treasuries on Wednesday and ahead of next week's key inflation report.

The September 10-year bond futures contract touched an intra-day contract high of 93.480 and the market now has its sights on the all time record of 93.630 set in early 1994. The instrument was first listed on the SFE in 1984.
A minor bounce in the Australia dollar also helped sentiment after its recent sustained weakness had prompted concerns that it might prevent a policy easing by the Reserve Bank.
The strong debt market rally kicked off in after hours trading as U.S. yields dropped on Wednesday following a modest 0.1 percent rise in the June CPI to an annual 2.3 percent.

However, domestic economists are expecting an even better outcome for Australia again when the second quarter CPI report is released next week, with estimates centring on flat for the quarter and just 0.6 percent annually.

Such a result, along with an expected 0.4 percent rise in the policy sensitive underlying inflation to a year-on-year rate of 1.7 percent, is seen compressing yield differentials to the U.S. even further.

Wednesday's U.S. data is seen lessening the chances of the Federal Reserve tightening in August, although the markets will get an update on the Fed's policy thinking when chairman Alan Greenspan delivers his Humphrey-Hawkins testimony next week.
Stable Fed rates would be one less hurdle for the RBA if it is considering easing and economists argue that local currency has yet to fall to a level that would prevent such a move.

"We expect the RBA will ease monetary conditions by announcing another rate cut within the next month, most likely after the June inflation report is released," said John Kyriakopoulos, senior economist at J.P. Morgan.

Australian/U.S. 10-year spread is closing in on last week's low of around 35 basis points, and the expected benign inflation report could see this tightening to major support at 25 b.p. New Zealand debt rebounded after Wednesday's weak performance and following a larger than expected fall in May retail sales.
